note: Robotic campaign missions. Transit time and launch windows are NOT stored here: scripts/campaign.gd computes them from physics.json (real orbit constants, tag std; Hohmann and synodic are calc). Everything below is a game rule (tag game) unless marked real. Gas-giant and outer-planet numbers are game values until the team adds them to the Data Book; replace them then.

gas_depths.name: Shallow skim
gas_depths.info: Low in the outer atmosphere. Small gain, almost no risk.

gas_depths.name: Mid-layer scoop
gas_depths.info: Deeper, more gas per pass, the probe feels the pressure.

gas_depths.name: Deep dip
gas_depths.info: Most gas, but one bad pass and the probe is lost.

probes.name: Mars Rover and Sample Return
probes.info: A robot rover lands by itself and collects rock samples. Light takes 3 to 22 minutes to reach Mars, so the landing must run without us.

probes.name: Venus Lander
probes.info: A short-lived lander in 465 C air and 90 times Earth pressure. The surface is very hostile.

probes.name: Mercury Orbiter
probes.info: An orbiter that keeps its place near the Sun. Hot day side, cold night side.

probes.name: Jupiter Gas Probe
probes.info: Dips into the gas giant and scoops air for the smelter.

probes.name: Saturn Gas Probe
probes.info: Samples Saturn's upper air. Rings are a hazard on the way in.

probes.name: Uranus Gas Probe
probes.info: Ice giant. Very cold air, so the scoop needs more care.

probes.name: Neptune Gas Probe
probes.info: The farthest planet. Light is about 4 hours away; the probe runs by itself on arrival.
